news.title: High number of new and inexperienced directors
news.body: There are 8 new directors who have joined the board in the last 3 years. The company's board is composed of: 8 new directors. No experienced directors. No highly experienced directors. MD & Director Jayshree Suresh Jain is the most experienced director on the board, commencing their role in 2024. The following issues are considered to be risks according to the Simply Wall St Risk Model: Lack of board continuity. Lack of experienced directors.

news.title: Covidh Technologies Limited Approves Directorate Appointments
news.body: Covidh Technologies Limited at its EGM held on April 2, 2026 approved the appointment of Mr. Dhairyasheel Vasantrao Yadav as an Executive Director of the Company; approved the appointment of Mr. Nandkumar Subhash Kadam as an Executive Director of the Company; approved the appointment of Mr. Pratap Dadasaheb Deshmuk as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director of the Company and approved the appointment of Ms Ritu Dhanraj Garad as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director of the Company.

news.title: Covidh Technologies Limited (BSE:534920) entered into a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Isera Biological Private Limited.
news.body:
Covidh Technologies Limited (BSE:534920) entered into a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Isera Biological Private Limited on February 23, 2026.

The proposed acquisition is subject to execution of definitive agreements, completion of satisfactory due diligence, receipt of necessary regulatory, statutory and shareholders' approvals, and fulfilment of agreed conditions precedent. Upon completion of the proposed transaction. iSERA shall become a wholly owned subsidiary of Covidh Technologies Limited.

news.title: New major risk - Shareholder dilution
news.body: The company's shareholders have been substantially diluted in the past year. Over 25x increase in shares outstanding. This is considered a major risk. Shareholder dilution occurs when there is an increase in the number of shares on issue that is not proportionally distributed between all shareholders. Often due to the company raising equity capital or some options being converted into stock. All else being equal, if there are more shares outstanding then each existing share will be entitled to a lower proportion of the company's total earnings, thus reducing earnings per share (EPS). While dilution might not always result in lower EPS (like if the company is using the capital to fund an EPS accretive acquisition) in a lot cases it does, along with lower dividends per share and less voting
